Article Title: Retired hurt after hit on wrist: Will Rishabh Pant bat on day 2 of Sri Lanka Test? India coach answers
Article Text:
Rishabh Pant gets medical attention (right), Pant walks off the field on day one of the second test between India and Sri Lanka, in Colombo. (PTI photo)

Will Pant bat on Day 2?

Padikkal’s century takes India to 300/5

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant retired hurt after being hit on his left arm during the opening day of the second Test against Sri Lanka in Colombo on Sunday.The incident happened during the third session when Sri Lanka fast bowler Lahiru Kumara bowled a short ball at Pant. The India batter tried to pull it behind square but missed, and the ball struck his left arm.Pant was in pain immediately after the blow and was attended to by the Indian team physiotherapist.An ice pack was first applied to his arm before it was taped. However, the tape was later removed as Pant continued to look uncomfortable.After scoring three runs from 15 balls, Pant walked off the field with the physiotherapist in the 58th over of India's innings.Ravindra Jadeja then came in to bat alongside Devdutt Padikkal.India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak said after the day's play that Pant is expected to continue in the match."I think he will be fine to continue tomorrow," he said in the post-day press conference on Day 1.Despite Pant's injury and wickets falling around him, Devdutt Padikkal scored 117 to guide India to 300/5 at stumps on the opening day.Dhruv Jurel was unbeaten on 7, while debutant Saransh Jain was unbeaten on 4 when play ended.Padikkal’s 168-ball innings, his second hundred in as many Tests, was not laced with the customary elegance barring on a couple of occasions when he brought out those full-blooded pulls and drives. He was dropped on 0 and 1 but remained solid after those reprieves.But the innings was still stunning because of the circumstances in which it was executed.
Article Summary: India wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant retired hurt after being hit on his left arm during the opening day of the second Test against Sri Lanka in Colombo. Pant was in pain immediately after the blow and was attended to by the Indian team physiotherapist. India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak said after the day's play that Pant is expected to continue in the match. Devdutt Padikkal scored 117 to guide India to 300/5 at stumps.

Article Title: No need to fake Kuldeep Yadav’s illness: Sitanshu Kotak
Article Text:
Kuldeep Yadav (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak firmly dismissed speculation surrounding Kuldeep Yadav ’s absence from the Colombo Test, insisting the left-arm wrist spinner was genuinely down with viral fever and there was “no need to fake” an illness to leave him out of the XI.“If the team needs a spinner and then he doesn’t play, there is no need to fake that he wasn’t keeping well,” Kotak said, stressing that Kuldeep was unfit to take the field.Kotak also provided a positive update on Rishabh Pant, who retired hurt on two after being struck on the left wrist by a Lahiru Kumara bouncer shortly after tea on Day 1. The wicketkeeper-batter received treatment before leaving the field, but Kotak said he was expected to resume his innings on Monday.India ended the day on 300/5 with Dhruv Jurel and Saransh Jain unbeaten, while hoping Pant’s return can help push the total higher.The opening day also saw tempers flare when Yashasvi Jaiswal and Sri Lanka pacer Asitha Fernando exchanged words following the opener’s dismissal. Kotak termed it a “heat of the moment” incident, though he felt Jaiswal should not have approached the bowler. Sri Lanka fast bowling coach Ryan van Niekerk called the confrontation an “overflow of emotion”, leaving any disciplinary action in the hands of match referee Andy Pycroft.
Article Summary: Kuldeep Yadav has been ruled out of the Colombo Test with viral fever. Rishabh Pant was struck on the wrist by a Lahiru Kumara bouncer on Day 1. India ended the day on 300/5 with Dhruv Jurel and Saransh Jain unbeaten.

Article Title: BWF World Championships: Alex Lanier makes history as France strikes twice; An Se-young wins again
Article Text:
France's Alex Lanier (PTI Photo)

Second world crown for An Se-young

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The shuttlecock hung in the air for a heartbeat, just long enough for Alex Lanier to measure destiny.The 21-year-old Frenchman unleashed a venomous, angled smash that kissed the hardwood before his opponent Kodai Naraoka could even flinch. As the winner landed, the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium arena erupted into a wall of sound. Lanier dropped his racket, leaped into the air in pure, unbridled euphoria, and went straight into a tearful embrace with his coach Kestutis Navickas.Standing atop the podium moments later with gold draped around his neck, he was all smiles. French badminton, so long an aspiring outsider, had finally conquered the world. On an unforgettable Sunday, Lanier etched his name into sporting folklore, becoming the first-ever singles badminton player from France to clinch the World Championship title.His historic triumph capped a watershed afternoon for French badminton. Moments before Lanier walked through the players’ tunnel, the French mixed doubles pair of Thom Gicquel and Delphine Delrue had already seized a sensational gold. Lanier carried the momentum of an entire nation’s breakthrough on his shoulders.Lanier’s march to the world crown was a showcase of breathtaking athleticism and nerve. The 21-year-old dismantled Japan’s world No.11 Kodai Naraoka 21-11, 21-11 in a lopsided 50-minute clinic.“It is a great day for French badminton and a great day for the whole staff,” Lanier said. “When the mixed gold was won, I just thought that I needed to give them a double smile and I needed to make history again.”The title clash began as a tense, toe-totoe duel, with former European champion Lanier holding a narrow 11-9 cushion at the mid-game interval. But from there, the Frenchman hit the gas. He took the opening game in 23 minutes. Naraoka attempted to dig deep in the second game, but the 25-year-old Japanese star soon ran out of steam. Lanier shut the door with punishing smashes to seal a comprehensive victory.The women’s singles final was a show of pure, indomitable will. Japan’s defending champion Akane Yamaguchi’s returns and jump smashes tested South Korea’s world No. 1 An Se-young at every turn. With the opening game locked in a nerve-wracking 17-17 deadlock, the 24-year-old South Korean dug deep to claim the opener 21-17 before prevailing in a series of high-speed rallies in the second game.Securing the 21-17, 21-14 victory in 49 minutes, An celebrated with a visceral victory cry.Yamaguchi becomes the first women’s singles player to capture six World Championship medals, but the day belonged to An Se-young, the flawless champion. With her second world title, the reigning Olympic champion accomplished a historic clean sweep. She holds the women’s singles crowns in the Olympics, World Championships, Asian Games and Asian Championships simultaneously.
Article Summary: Alex Lanier becomes the first-ever singles badminton player from France to clinch the World Championship title. The 21-year-old dismantled Japan’s world No.11 Kodai Naraoka 21-11, 21- 11 in a lopsided 50-minute clinic.

Article Title: Duleep Trophy starts with a question mark on relevance
Article Text:
Duleep Trophy (ANI Photo)

After

BCCI

dissolves national selectors’ role in picking zonal teams, sanctity of the tournament comes under scanner

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

CHENNAI/NEW DELHI: A few days before the Duleep Trophy got underway at the Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru on Sunday, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia announced that the final will be shifted to MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai. The reason given was that there will be fans who will come to watch the match, which doesn’t happen in the CoE.Chennai is a cricket-crazy centre. But when you ask those who ‘book’ their IPL tickets long before the event, whether they would be interested in attending the Duleep final, the standard query is: “Will Shubman Gill play?”Gill, in this case, stands for all the stars of Indian cricket. The Duleep final is from Sept 6-10, and it will be interesting to see that those who are not part of the Afghanistan T20 series starting on Sept 12 turn out at MAC.That said, the primary purpose of the inter-zonal tournament is to check out the best performers in the Ranji Trophy go head-to-head against each other. The relevance of the tournament, especially after the inception of IPL, has diminished drastically. Yet, it remains a stepping stone for a lot of players.The tournament’s sanctity has been up for debate with the selection process. The BCCI, in the last decade, has often tried playing the tournament with national selectors picking the India ‘A’, ‘B’ and ‘C’ teams.This year, the board has reverted to the inter-zonal format and has kept the national selectors out of the equation. The result? Delhi opener Sanat Sangwan, who scored 828 runs in seven Ranji Trophy matches, was on Sunday, benched by the North Zone management and instead middle-order batter Yash Dhull was played as an opener. The Central Zone team has only one player from semifinalist Uttarakhand while Madhya Pradesh was the only team from the zone to have qualified for the quarterfinals. There have been a few debatable selections in the South Zone team as well.Former national selector Devang Gandhi believes that a national selector has to be involved in the selection process if the sanctity of the tournament is to be saved. “When we were selectors from 2016-2021, BCCI had given us the responsibility of picking the Duleep Trophy to maintain continuity in a player’s development. If the opener with the highest runs in the country doesn’t get to play Duleep Trophy, it defeats the purpose of the tournament. The board must at least ensure one selector from each zone is present in planning their respective zonal teams. Otherwise, politics at the state association level can crop up. There’s no accountability if BCCI selectors are not used,” Gandhi told TOI.“Today we are seeing Manav Suthar and Saransh Jain as products of domestic cricket. If that structure is compromised, then it will be difficult to see such journeys,” Gandhi added.TOI understands that the selection committee has been asking for a greater role in Duleep Trophy teams. The board had given the Ajit Agarkar-led committee the responsibility for the last two years before handing complete authority to state associations in the zone.For selectors, Duleep is a tournament from where players for India ‘A’ are selected. In this case, Australia ‘A’ will come to India in October and those who are part of this Duleep, will look to stake a claim in the ‘A’ side. It is definitely a step lower for the established stars and there’s not much to prove for them, unless it’s just a test of fitness, as is the case for Washington Sundar or Sai Sudharsan, who are coming back from injuries.In recent times, we have often seen T20 performances have often been the benchmark for red-ball selection. Ajinkya Rahane came back into India’s WTC Final squad in 2023 on the basis of a great IPL while Sai Sudharsan’s entry into the Test squad has largely been due to his consistency in IPL for Gujarat Titans.When we look at the East Zone squad that took on NorthEast from Sunday, we see Vaibhav Sooryavanshi being named as the vice-captain ahead of Abhimanyu Easwaran. The Bengal opener has an average of 47.85 over 112 games while Sooryavanshi averages 17.25 in the eight games that he has played.While it can raise a few eyebrows, Gandhi says it’s “a question of backing talent”. “Nothing against Abhimanyu, but we all know what Vaibhav brings to the table. He is one for the future with incredible talent and what’s the harm if he is put in the leadership group at a young age. The selectors will know how he reacts to it,” Gandhi said.
Article Summary: The Duleep Trophy final will be held at MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai. BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia announced that there will be fans who will come to watch the match, which doesn't happen in the CoE. The tournament’s sanctity has been up for debate with the selection process.

Article Title: Duleep Trophy: Kotian, Deshpande turn up the heat; North Zone fold for 251; East thrive
Article Text:
Tanush Kotian (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

VAIBHAV FAILS; GHARAMI & SHAHBAZ SHINE

Brief scores:

North Zone 251 in 66.5 overs (Ayush Doseja 42, Ayush Badoni 51, Anshul Kamboj 60; Tanush Kotian 4-72, Tushar Deshpande 4-57) vs West Zone 31/2 in 10 overs

East Zone 355/6 in 80 overs ( Kumar Kushagra 55, Sudip Gharami 146, Shahbaz Ahmed 100 batting) vs North East Zone.

BENGALURU: The domestic season may have just begun, but Tanush Kotian looked anything but rusty. The West Zone off-spinner hit his lengths from the outset, extracted drift from the dry surface and bowled with the confidence of a man who knows there is an India spot to chase.Kotian (4/72), alongside medium-pacer Tushar Deshpande (4/57), helped West Zone bowl out North Zone for 251 on the opening day of the Duleep Trophy at the BCCI Centre of Excellence here on Sunday. West were 31/2 at stumps.Kotian’s spell was a study in patience and control. He refused to be distracted when the batters attacked him. The Mumbai allrounder had travelled to Sri Lanka as India’s net bowler ahead of the ongoing Test series, and the experience of bowling to quality batters has surely sharpened him ahead of a busy season.Having already represented India A and earned a maiden call-up to the senior side, Kotian knows another consistent domestic campaign could bring him closer to the India cap. “I have that one step (in my mind) — to represent India. I have to do better with every opportunity I get. Getting those four wickets or scoring 50s or 100s is what I need to do more. I have been doing that for Mumbai,” said Kotian, who has taken 61 wickets and scored 902 runs in his last three Ranji seasons.“With the mentality I have, I always think of doing well in both bowling and batting. Selectors have their thing; if they have to select me, they will. I have to take wickets and make runs for my team and do better,” he added.Kotian’s first three-over spell went wicketless. He got his reward in the 49th over when he dismissed Ayush Doseja. In his next over, he trapped Kanhaiya Wadhawan leg before, reducing North Zone to 155/6.Even when Anshul Kamboj (60) attacked him with a couple of sixes, Kotian was brave enough to continue flighting the ball. Kamboj eventually became his fourth victim.Deshpande played his part too, removing key batters Ayush Badoni (52) and Kotian’s job, though, is far from over. With West Zone two down, Monday will offer him another opportunity to underline his value as an all-rounder.At the adjacent ground, much of the attention was on 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi as East Zone took on Northeast Zone. The teenager struck two fours in his six-ball stay but was dismissed in the second over.The experienced Sudip Gharami, however, made the most of his opportunity, scoring 146 (185b, 25x4, 1x6), while Shahbaz Ahmed was unbeaten on 100 (137b, 9x4, 2x6) as East Zone reached 355/6 at stumps.
Article Summary: West Zone bowl out North Zone for 251 on the opening day of the Duleep Trophy at the BCCI Centre of Excellence here on Sunday. Off-spinner Tanush Kotian (4/72) and medium-pacer Tushar Deshpande (4-57) took two wickets each.

NEW DELHI: India made one change to their playing XI for the second Test against Sri Lanka in Colombo on Sunday, with Kuldeep Yadav missing out after failing to fully recover from a viral infection and Saransh Jain making his Test debut India captain Shubman Gill won the toss and elected to bat first, with the hosts also handing Test debuts to Kamil Mishara and Pasindu Sooriyabandara.India entered the second Test with an unassailable 1-0 lead after their 165-run victory in the series opener at Galle. However, Kuldeep's absence meant India had to alter their combination, with Jain coming into the XI as the spin-bowling allrounder.The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) confirmed that Kuldeep remains unavailable for selection but could still be used in a specific situation."Mr Kuldeep Yadav has not fully recovered from his viral illness. He was unavailable for selection in the Playing XI for the second Test against Sri Lanka. However, he can take the field as a concussion substitute, if required," the BCCI said.Gill also addressed Kuldeep's absence after winning the toss, confirming that an infection had ruled out the left-arm wristspinner."[Playing XI] Kuldeep, unfortunately, had some infections, so he misses out, and Saransh makes his debut for India," Gill said.With Kuldeep unavailable, Jain received his first opportunity at Test level. The 33-year-old was presented his India cap by Ravindra Jadeja during the team's huddle before the start of play.Jain becomes the first India player to make his international debut after turning 33 since Robin Singh in 1998.Gill opted to bat after assessing the Colombo surface and felt it offered better batting conditions than the pitch in Galle."Batting first, yes. [On the pitch] It looks like a much harder, much better surface compared to Galle. Galle was also a very good wicket, but I think as the game went on, it got a little bit slower and the ball started to turn. We're expecting the same, but I think for the first two or three days, I think it'll be a really good wicket to bat on," Gill said.Reflecting on India's dominant win in the first Test, Gill rated the team's performance highly but admitted there was still room for improvement."[How he would rate the Galle win] I would say probably a nine, because there's always room for improvement, and I think we played a pretty good match, a decent match. And obviously there were some areas where we could have got a little bit better, but, you know, this is Test cricket. It's very, very difficult to be able to have a near-perfect game because you're playing for five days, and to play that dominant and consistent cricket, especially in Test, is hard. But I think overall we had a pretty good match," Gill said.
Article Summary: India captain Shubman Gill opts to bat first in second Test against Sri Lanka. Kuldeep Yadav misses out after failing to fully recover from a viral infection. Saransh Jain makes his Test debut after turning 33 years old. Kamil Mishara and Pasindu Sooriyabandara also handed Test debuts.

Article Title: Abinaya Rajarajan breaks U20 national record with stunning 11.34s in Bhubaneswar
Article Text:
Abinaya Rajarajan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bhubaneswar: Abinaya Rajarajan’s comeback from injury had been a gradual one, with the 19-year-old Tamil Nadu sprinter steadily improving with every competition.On Saturday, she produced the breakthrough she had been waiting for, clocking a stunning 11.34s to win the women’s 100m title and break the U20 national record at the World Athletics Continental Tour Silver meet at Kalinga Stadium here.Abinaya bettered the previous mark of 11.53s set by Nipam Chauhan at the U20 Federation Cup earlier this year, capping a steady progression since returning from an injury that kept her out of training for nearly four months.“In the Czech Republic, I ran 11.58s. I was hoping to break the national record there, but because of my physical condition, I couldn’t do it,” said the 19-year-old, who trains at NCOE Trivandrum under coach R Seenivasan and is currently the third fastest India after Dutee Chand (11.17s) and Rachita Mistry (11.34s).“But today I was fully fired up. I really wanted to run and break the under-20 national record. I didn’t expect this, though. 11.34 is a crazy, crazy time.”Abinaya had suffered the injury during the Asian Indoor Championships earlier this year and was forced to withdraw from the final. She then underwent an extended rehabilitation before gradually returning to competition. Her timings improved with every race, but the U20 national record remained elusive.Her father, however, had spotted her natural speed much earlier.“We had a running race when we were out for a walk, and she beat me when she was six years old. Initially, I thought it was a fluke. The next day, I ran with full effort, but she was still faster than me. That’s when I realised she was talented,” said Rajarajan.While the words of her coach and the support of her father helped her through the difficult period, visualization also played a big role in her recovery.“Visualization was obviously a big part of it. I also kept thinking about the words of my coach during training. And my dad was a huge support. He has always been my hero,” said Abinaya. “Even when I was doing visualization, he would tell me, ‘Don’t take any pressure. Run easily. Just run. Enjoy. I love you.’”And after finally producing the run, she had been chasing, Abinaya celebrated with Cristiano Ronaldo’s famous ‘Siu’ celebration to the delight of the fans. Abinaya’s record-breaking run apart, it was a strong day for Indian athletics.Rohit Yadav put his Commonwealth Games disappointment behind him to win the men’s javelin title with a huge 87.68m throw in his final attempt, having taken a fall during his second attempt. Yashvir Singh, who won bronze at the CWG, finished second with a best throw of 82.94m.Among the other big names of Indian athletics, Ancy Sojan won the women’s long jump with a best leap of 6.71m, while Shaili Singh came second with an effort of 6.56m. Murali Sreeshankar clinched the men’s title with an effort of 8.07m, while Vithya Ramraj won the women’s 400m with a personal best of 51.96s.In the men’s 100m, Animesh Kujur and Gurindervir Singh clocked 10.32s and 10.39s respectively.Among the foreign athletes, Nigeria’s Commonwealth Games shot put champion Chukwuebuka Enekwechi won the title with a throw of 20.78m. In the women’s discus throw, Jamaica’s Commonwealth Games champion Samantha Hall finished second with a throw of 58.43m, while Brazil’s Andressa de Morais won with a penultimate-round throw of 58.66m.However, it was a disappointing night for Jyothi Yarraji, who finished third in the women’s 100m hurdles with a time of 13.24s and later pulled out midway into the 100m.
Article Summary: Abinaya Rajarajan clocked 11.34s to win the women’s 100m title and break the U20 national record at the World Athletics Continental Tour Silver meet at Kalinga Stadium. The 19-year-old Tamil Nadu sprinter had suffered an injury that kept her out of training for nearly four months. Abinaya is currently the third fastest India after Dutee Chand (11.17s) and Rachita Mistry.

Article Title: India face must-win Australia clash, need Netherlands favour to keep World Cup dream alive
Article Text:
​India face Australia with semis in sight​

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

“Remember, Red, hope is a good thing, maybe the best of things, and no good thing ever dies.”Those famous closing words from ‘The Shawshank Redemption’ could well be the Indian women’s hockey team’s mantra as they chase a place in the World Cup semifinals against all odds.After going down to the Netherlands in their last match following another brave performance, India will have to beat Australia on Sunday in their second game of Pool E and hope that China lose to Netherlands in the other group game.Considering how Netherlands have played so far, beating China doesn’t seem like an improbable task. But China, too, haven’t been pushovers. They have remained unbeaten in the tournament so far and gave the Dutch a run for their money at the Olympics final. In their last four Pro League meetings, however, the Dutch have completely dominated them, and India would want that trend to continue on Sunday.But rather than thinking too much about what may or may not happen in that match, India will have to focus on their own game against the Aussies.“Our focus has to remain on ourselves because we have one very important match, and we are ready for it,” skipper Salima Tete said. “We have to give everything we have because it’s our last match, against Australia, and we have to treat it like a final.We have a chance, and that’s what I keep telling the team.”So far, India have held China to a 2-2 draw, beaten South Africa 6-1, held England to a goalless draw and gone down to Netherlands 0-2. Their unbeaten streak may have come to an end on Friday night, but they put up another impressive showing and, if they can maintain that level against the Aussies, a win is certainly not beyond them.Interestingly, India played four practice matches against Australia this year and did well against a team in transition. They lost the first match, won the second in a shoot-out after it finished 1-1 in regulation time, beat the hosts 2-0 in the third and then went down 2-3 in the fourth.Speaking about Sunday’s match, India coach Sjoerd Marijne said, “We see it as a quarterfinal. It’s always very close (against Australia), and that’s how I think the match on Sunday will be. There will not be many secrets because we play many times against each other.”Having said that, the coach will still hope for one major change — India converting their chances. While they have been disciplined in defence, they haven’t been able to maintain the same discipline in front of goal.“Against big teams, if you get three opportunities, you have to convert one or two. That’s something we keep working on,” said the Dutchman. “It’s the same with penalty corners. At the moment we are not scoring off a lot of penalty corners…and we know that.But we have the quality, and I have confidence in Navneet (Kaur) and Deepika.”And perhaps that is where India’s biggest challenge — and their biggest opportunity — lies. They have shown they can stay in the contest against the best in the world. On Sunday, they will need to turn that resilience into goals.India have done their bit before against the odds. Now, they need one more big performance — and a little help from Netherlands — to keep their World Cup dream alive.
Article Summary: India will have to beat Australia on Sunday in their second game of Pool E and hope that China lose to Netherlands in the other group game. India have held China to a 2-2 draw, beaten South Africa 6-1, held England to a goalless draw and gone down to Netherlands 0-2.

Article Title: Treesa Jolly-Gayatri Gopichand end India’s 15-year wait, assure World Championships medal
Article Text:
India's Gayatri Gopichand Pullela, right, and Treesa Jolly (AP Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand secured a World Championships medal after producing a superb comeback victory over China’s Jia Yi Fan and Zhang Shu Xian in the women’s doubles quarterfinals on Friday.The unseeded Indian pair fought for 69 minutes before overcoming their Chinese opponents 16-21, 21-15, 21-13 to book their place in the last four. The victory guarantees Treesa and Gayatri at least a bronze medal at the championships.Their achievement is particularly significant for Indian women’s doubles badminton. The country’s last World Championships medal in the event came in 2011, when Jwala Gutta and Ashwini Ponnappa claimed bronze in London.Backed by strong home support, Treesa and Gayatri recovered from a slow start and gradually took control of the contest. After dropping the opening game, the Indians sharpened their attacking play, finding greater success with their smashes and producing cleaner work around the net.The semifinal appearance marks another major milestone for a pair that has already enjoyed success on the international circuit.Treesa and Gayatri reached the All England Open semifinals in consecutive years in 2022 and 2023. They also won bronze at the 2022 Commonwealth Games and broke into the world’s top 10 at the beginning of last year.Their progress was interrupted earlier this year when Treesa suffered a serious ankle injury during training ahead of the Asia Badminton Championships and Uber Cup.The injury occurred when Treesa accidentally stepped on Gayatri’s foot during practice and twisted her ankle. An MRI subsequently revealed two high-grade muscle tears and two ligament tears, forcing her into a lengthy rehabilitation programme.The pair eventually began their comeback at the Indonesia Open before competing at the US Open. They then won the Philippine International Challenge earlier this month, providing further evidence that they were returning to their best.Now, that comeback has reached its biggest moment yet, with Treesa and Gayatri assured of a place on the World Championships podium.

The unseeded Indian pair fought for 69 minutes before overcoming their Chinese opponents 16-21, 21-15,21-13 to book their place in the last four. The victory guarantees Treesa and gayatri at least a bronze medal at the championships.

(Aarav Dengla is India’s 93rd Grandmaster. He is a keen observer and student of world history in general and chess history in particular.)

Long before ‘artificial intelligence’ became a regular part of the everyday lexicon, Amazon came up with the concept of “artificial artificial intelligence,” or, in other words, work that appeared to be automated but, in reality, was completed by humans.Amazon brought this type of work to the masses via its crowdsourcing marketplace called Mechanical Turk. Launched in 2005, the marketplace offered up a wide variety of tasks that humans were still better at completing than their computer-based counterparts.Mechanical Turk got its name from an 18th-century chess-playing machine that had appeared to play the game of chess with great intelligence and skill.The Mechanical Turk first appeared in 1770, when the inventor and civil servant Wolfgang von Kempelen showed his contraption to the Habsburg court of Empress Maria Theresa. The contraption had a large wooden figure, dressed in Ottoman robes, sitting behind a large cabinet with a chessboard on top.It was presented as a machine that could think and play against a human. Over the next eight decades, dotted with long dormant stretches, it would tour Europe and the Americas and would play against prominent figures such as Benjamin Franklin and Napoleon Bonaparte.The Turk was not an autonomous machine. A skilled chess player sat inside the cabinet and operated its moves.Magnetic chess pieces allowed the operator to follow the game on the board above, and a system of levers transmitted the operator’s movements to the mannequin’s arm.The cabinet created for the demonstration was designed to deceive the spectators. During the demonstration, the doors of the cabinet would be opened to reveal rows of gears and other machinery. The operator used a system of sliding panels and a movable seat to remain hidden at those moments. The cramped arrangement was physically demanding for the operator.Following the death of Kempelen in 1804, the Turk was sold to Johann Mälzel. Several leading chess players are known to have operated the Turk. Johann Baptist Allgaier is credited with being the operator during the game against Napoleon in 1809.In later exhibitions in Britain, the Turk was operated by Jacques François Mouret and William Lewis. The principal operator of the Turk during Mälzel’s tours of the United States was William Schlumberger. However, the identities of the operators for von Kempelen’s earliest exhibitions of the Turk remain unknown to this day.The obvious question is why so many successful chess players in the early 19th century would endure such punishing surroundings and play hidden in a machine. The answer lies in how even elite chess players struggled to make a living otherwise.They were offered generous pay for operating the Turk, which playing the game itself rarely provided. Earnings from coaching, exhibition games and occasional stake-matches were limited and inconsistent and not enough to support a living. Operating the Turk therefore offered steady and reliable income, even though it required secrecy, travel, and long periods inside a claustrophobic cabinet.The Turk remained the subject of suspicion throughout. In an essay published in 1836, Edgar Allan Poe noted that a machine should make moves at regular intervals while the Turk’s timing varied, which mirrored the human way of playing. Poe concluded that a human was involved, but he could not pin down how.The first full and reliable account came in 1857, less than three years after the original Turk was destroyed in a fire, when Silas Weir Mitchell, son of the last private owner of the Turk, published a detailed account.That the Turk endured for so long despite widespread skepticism is the fascinating bit. Solving the riddle of how it worked was part of the attraction. Its long existence coincided with an age of rapid mechanization when people were beginning to ask which forms of human labor might be reproduced by machines.Amazon’s Mechanical Turk borrowed the old illusion’s central idea: a process can look automated but, in reality, require human effort to complete. While the comparison isn’t perfect, it does give us a sense of how new technologies can first appear to do something and, when we look closer, reveal hidden human labor behind them.In our current era of rapid advances in artificial intelligence, it’s too early to predict exactly how far artificial intelligence will go, or whether synthetic systems will ever be able to fully replace human thought. The Turk, in short, is just a reminder of how the impression of an autonomous mind can hide the reality behind it.
Article Summary: Mechanical Turk got its name from an 18th-century chess-playing machine that had appeared to play the game of chess with great intelligence and skill. Over the next eight decades, dotted with long dormant stretches, it would play against prominent figures such as Benjamin Franklin and Napoleon Bonaparte.

Article Title: Men’s Hockey World Cup: How can India qualify for the semifinals? The permutations explained
Article Text:
India's players during the FIH World Cup. (AP/PTI Photo)

What India need to do against Argentina

Why India need a big Dutch favour

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India's hopes of reaching the semifinals of the FIH Men's Hockey World Cup 2026 are hanging by a thread after their second-round defeat to the Netherlands, but Argentina's 3-1 win over England has kept Craig Fulton's side mathematically alive.India suffered a 1-3 loss to the Netherlands on Saturday, leaving them bottom of Pool E with no points from their two matches. However, England's defeat to Argentina later in the day opened a narrow route to the last four.The equation is now simple in principle, although the margins are anything but: India must beat Argentina and then hope the Netherlands defeat England by a sufficiently large margin.India must beat Argentina by at least two goals in their final Pool E match on Monday.A two-goal victory would give India three points and allow them to move above Argentina on goals scored, provided the relevant goal-difference calculations remain level. A victory by more than two goals would give India the advantage on goal difference.The task, however, is easier said than done. Argentina have already beaten India twice in the FIH Pro League this year, winning 8-0 and 4-2.India therefore need not only a victory but a convincing one to keep their semifinal hopes alive.Even if India beat Argentina, their qualification will depend on the result of Netherlands vs England.The Dutch are already top of Pool E with six points and a goal difference of +4, while England and Argentina have three points each with goal differences of zero. India have zero points and a -4 goal difference after conceding seven goals and scoring three.The safest route for India is a two-goal win over Argentina combined with a three-goal victory for the Netherlands against England.For example, if India beat Argentina 3-1 and England lose 0-3 to the Netherlands, India would finish ahead of England on goal difference and eliminate Argentina. The Netherlands would top the pool with nine points, leaving India second.Some results could produce further tie-break complications. If India win 3-1 and England lose 1-3, both would have identical goals scored and conceded, meaning the field-goal tie-break could come into play.India currently have one field goal in the pool, Dilpreet Singh's strike against England, while England have three.The final-day schedule adds another twist. India play Argentina at 6:30pm IST on Monday, while England face the Netherlands at 10:30pm IST.That means England will know exactly what they need from their match against the Dutch based on India's result earlier in the evening.
Article Summary: India must beat Argentina by at least two goals in their final Pool E match on Monday. India suffered a 1-3 loss to the Netherlands on Saturday, leaving them bottom of Pool E with no points from their two matches. England's defeat to Argentina later in the day opened a narrow route to the last four. India play Argentina at 6:30pm IST on Monday, while England face the Netherlands.

Article Title: Another nightclub incident hits England: Fast bowler handcuffed, detained by police; ECB launches probe

England fast bowler Brydon Carse is under investigation after an incident at a nightclub in Derby on Saturday, the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) said on Sunday.Videos circulating on social media appeared to show Carse being led away from a club in handcuffs by four police officers. Carse, who is part of England's squad for the second Test against Pakistan, was seen outside a nightclub in Derby.Durham and England teammate Matthew Potts was seen speaking to Carse, while former England captain Ben Stokes also appeared in the background.Carse was briefly detained at the scene but was not arrested, according to The Telegraph. He returned to the team hotel soon afterwards."We are aware of an incident which is reported to have taken place in Derby last night, and are currently investigating," the ECB said in a statement."We will provide a further update when possible."Carse and Potts had played for Durham earlier on Saturday as they beat Derbyshire by 338 runs in a second-division County Championship match in Derby.Carse, 31, has played 14 Tests and was included in England's squad for the first two Tests of the three-match series against Pakistan. He did not feature in the opening Test at Headingley, where England lost by an innings and 103 runs inside three days.The second Test at Lord's starts on Thursday.The incident comes amid a series of off-field episodes involving England players over the past year.The most serious involved Test vice-captain Harry Brook, who was punched by a nightclub bouncer in Wellington in the early hours of November 1 last year, shortly before he was due to lead England in an ODI against New Zealand.During the Ashes, a mid-series break in Noosa also drew attention to the players' drinking.More recently, Stokes and Gus Atkinson stayed out beyond England's new midnight curfew after the first Test against New Zealand this summer. Both were stood down for the following Test at The Oval as part of a disciplinary process.Stokes retired from Test cricket at the end of that series and was replaced as captain by Joe Root, who had previously led England from 2017 to 2022.One of Root's first decisions after returning to the role was to remove the curfew and tell his players to "be adults".
Article Summary: England fast bowler Brydon Carse under investigation after incident at a nightclub in Derby. Carse was briefly detained at the scene but was not arrested, according to The Telegraph. Videos circulating on social media appeared to show Carse being led away from a club in handcuffs by four police officers.

Article Title: Devdutt Padikkal aces SSC Test: Second successive ton anchors India despite Rishabh Pant injury scare
Article Text:
India's Devdutt Padikkal celebrates his century. (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

On a day packed with drama, injuries and confrontations, Devdutt Padikkal once again emerged as India’s man of the moment. The tall left-hander continued his dream run in Sri Lanka, crafting a gritty second successive century to steer India to 300 for five on a hard-fought opening day of the second and final Test at the Sinhalese Sports Club on Sunday.The Karnataka skipper’s 117 off 193 balls was worth far more than the score suggested. On a livelier SSC surface offering bounce and movement, Padikkal held India’s innings together after the visitors lost wickets at crucial moments and suffered a scare when Rishabh Pant retired hurt after being struck on the forearm by a Lahiru Kumara delivery.Padikkal’s form has been a major positive for India. Drafted in at No. 3 in place of Sai Sudharsan for this series, he has now amassed 328 runs in three innings at an average of 109.33, following scores of 167, 44 and 117. He had also scored an unbeaten century in the warm-up game, strengthening his case to retain his spot when Sudharsan returns.India’s day began brightly after skipper Shubman Gill opted to bat. Yashasvi Jaiswal looked in sublime touch, racing to 45 off 53 balls with nine boundaries. The left-hander punished Kumara early and unfurled some trademark drives before falling against the run of play to Asitha Fernando, who breached his defence with a superb nip-backer.The dismissal sparked controversy. Fer nando gave Jaiswal an animated send-off and the opener turned back, exchanging words with the pacer before the pair came face-to-face. At one point, Jaiswal’s helmet brushed Fernando’s forehead before Sri Lanka captain Dhananjaya de Silva stepped in to defuse the tension. Earlier, KL Rahul had contributed 18 before edging Kumara behind the wicket after helping India reach 37.With India at 66 for two, Padikkal and Gill rebuilt calmly. The pair added 120 runs for the third wicket, blunting Sri Lanka’s attack through the afternoon. Gill looked set for another substantial contribution and reached his ninth Test fifty, while also crossing the milestone of 3,000 Test runs in his 43rd match. However, the India captain could not capitalise, edging Fernando to wicketkeeper Niroshan Dickwella for 50.India’s troubles deepened soon after when Pant, attempting a pull shot against Kumara, was struck painfully on the forearm and retired hurt on three.That left Padikkal with the responsibility of guiding the innings, and he responded admirably. Having survived two early chances, dropped on nought by Sonal Dinusha and again on one by Dhananjaya de Silva, he made Sri Lanka pay. Unlike his fluent 167 at Galle, this was an innings built on patience and discipline. Padikkal negotiated the seamers carefully, rotated strike efficiently and punished loose deliveries from the spinners.He found valuable support from Ravindra Jadeja , who contributed 43 in a 74-run fifth-wicket stand that steadied India after Pant’s exit. Padikkal eventually reached his century with a composed single off Prabath Jayasuriya before Keshara Nuwantha finally ended his resistance with a delivery that spun sharply to hit the stumps.Jadeja too looked set for a fifty before Fernando produced another peach that jagged back from round the stumps to castle him.Fernando was Sri Lanka’s standout bowler, finishing with three for 46 from 16 impressive overs, while Kumara claimed one wicket and consistently troubled the batters with his pace and his shortball tactic. Earlier in the day, India handed a Test debut to 33-year-old off-spinner Saransh Jain after Kuldeep Yadav was ruled out with a viral infection. Jain, became the first Indian off-spinner to make his Test debut since Washington Sundar in 2021.
Article Summary: Devdutt Padikkal scored 117 off 193 balls to guide India to 300 for five. Rishabh Pant retired hurt after being struck on the forearm by a Lahiru Kumara delivery. Yashasvi Jaiswal looked in sublime touch, racing to 45 off 53 balls.

Article Title: ECB launches investigation into Brydon Carse after England pacer seen in handcuffs outside nightclub
Article Text:
Brydon Carse under ECB investigation

The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) has launched an investigation into England fast bowler Brydon Carse after footage emerged on social media showing him being led away in handcuffs by police outside a nightclub in Derby. The incident reportedly occurred late on Saturday, August 22, after Carse joined his Durham teammates for celebrations following their 338-run County Championship victory over Derbyshire.Videos circulating on social media show Carse surrounded by police officers outside a busy nightclub, with four officers appearing to escort the England pacer away in handcuffs. Durham teammates Matthew Potts and Ben Stokes were also present at the scene, with Potts seen attempting to speak to Carse.According to The Telegraph, Carse was briefly detained but was not arrested. He was subsequently released and returned to the Durham team hotel. The circumstances that led to police intervention remain unclear, and there has been no official confirmation about whether Carse was involved in any altercation.The incident could have implications for Carse's England future. The fast bowler was released from the national squad to play for Durham after missing the first Test against Pakistan at Headingley, but remains part of England's squad for the second Test at Lord's, beginning on August 27.Carse is due to rejoin the England camp on Monday. The ECB and Cricket Regulator are understood to be gathering information before deciding whether any further action is required."We are aware of an incident which is reported to have taken place in Derby last night, and are currently investigating," the ECB said in a statement."We will provide a further update when possible."The investigation comes just days after England Test captain Joe Root called on his players to set a better example following the start of his second stint as Test captain."You always want to represent your country in the best possible light," Root told BBC Sport."We might have fallen short of that on a few occasions in the recent past. The only thing we can do to rectify that is be really good role models, good human beings and put in really strong performances on the field," he added.
Article Summary: England fast bowler Brydon Carse is under investigation by the ECB. Carse was seen being led away in handcuffs by police outside a nightclub in Derby. The incident reportedly occurred late on Saturday, August 22, after Carse joined his Durham teammates for celebrations following their County Championship victory.

Article Title: Rest, viral and not in India's XI for Colombo Test: The mysterious case of Kuldeep Yadav

Kuldeep Yadav

"I don't think this is a relevant question..." was India's batting coach Sitanshu Kotak's response, after a pause, when he was asked whether Kuldeep Yadav would have played had he been fit. Kotak further explained the timeline of events and asserted that the chinaman was unavailable due to a "viral" illness and had been experiencing some discomfort since the team left Galle after the series opener."He genuinely had viral when he left from there (Galle). If the team needs an off-spinner, there is no need to say that he (Kuldeep) isn't well. If the guy is in no position to play, there is no point thinking about what would have been done if he would have been fit. He has recovered reasonably well. He looked good when I met him in the evening. So it came down to whether we need three fast bowlers or three spinners. And with them having four left-handers in the top order, it made sense to play an off-spinner."Interestingly, different versions regarding Kuldeep have emerged from the Indian camp over the last 72 hours. Spin-bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule was specifically asked about the chinaman and KL Rahul missing the team's first practice session in Colombo on August 21, but he said they were "resting".Kuldeep did travel with the team and was also spotted in the dugout alongside Sarfaraz Khan. The official word from the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) remains "viral illness"."Mr Kuldeep Yadav has not fully recovered from his viral illness. He was unavailable for selection in the Playing XI for the second Test against Sri Lanka. However, he can take the field as a concussion substitute, if required," read a BCCI statement after the toss.Captain Shubman Gill was the first to reveal Kuldeep's illness when he was asked about the change in the Playing XI.
Article Summary: Kuldeep Yadav unavailable due to a "viral" illness. India handed a debut to 33-year-old Saransh Jain. The official word from the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) remains 'viral illness'

India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak has reacted to the heated exchange between Yashasvi Jaiswal and Sri Lanka pacer Asitha Fernando during the opening day of the second Test in Colombo. Kotak said such incidents can happen in the heat of the moment, but felt that Jaiswal should not have gone so close to the Sri Lankan bowler.Jaiswal and Fernando were involved in a tense confrontation during the first session on Sunday.The India opener was batting well on 45 when Fernando dismissed him in the 17th over. Her sole aim is to pull off the one like Sharmila Dhankar, India's Commonwealth Games shot put gold medallist.Before the 2026 CWG campaign, she, like many of us, had almost certainly never heard the name. And it's not because Dhankar had not won anything before the Glasgow Games; she had, a gold medal in the Women's Shot Put F57 event at the 2026 Fazza International Para Athletics Championship, but because one of the primary institutions whose entire job was to carry that story back from the medal podium to villages and training grounds across the state has, for all practical purposes, gone quiet.That's the part of this story that rarely gets told. India walked away from Glasgow with 39 medals, and for a week, the athletes who won them were everywhere, garlanded at airports, seated beside ministers, their faces on the evening news. But medals don't build the next generation of athletes by themselves. Somebody has to keep telling their stories, long after the felicitation photo is filed away, to the kid training in a dusty school ground who needs proof that this path actually leads somewhere.We wanted to know which state sports departments are still doing their job of promoting the sports and their grassroots on their social media platforms, and which ones seem to have simply logged off. So we scrolled through the timelines ourselves. Here's what we found.No state produced more glory in Glasgow than Haryana. Eleven medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze, spanning boxing, wrestling, athletics, and para sport, headlined by a Neeraj Chopra silver that will be replayed on sports channels for years.Alongside him were names most of India still had little knowledge of. The likes of Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Sachin Siwach, and Ankush Panghal, all of whom trained in government facilities, under government schemes, and who'd probably appreciate their own state department cheering as loudly for them as it does for its concert lineups.Because that's the thing. The Sports Department, Government of Haryana's X account has posted exactly once in all of 2026, and it's a flyer for the music acts playing at the Chief Minister's Cup.Facebook and Instagram follow a similar rhythm with a short cluster of posts around that February event, and then not much else.Eleven medals, and not one dedicated post to show for it. Somewhere in Rohtak or Bhiwani, a young pugilist training in Priya Ghanghas's discipline would probably just like a little proof that someone up top is paying attention.Manipur's page has an odd time-capsule quality to it. This is the state that gave India Mirabai Chanu, one of the country's most beloved Olympic medalists, and this Commonwealth Games alone produced four medalists from Manipur, Chanu's gold among them, alongside Rishikanta Singh, Bindyarani Devi, and Jadumani Singh.And yet the Department of Youth Affairs & Sports' X account hasn't posted since October 2023, a "Run for Unity" event, frozen well before any of this year's medals happened.Although the Facebook page has had a few sporadic posts here and there this year, its Instagram account has managed just two posts since January. It’s the kind of gap that makes you wonder if someone simply forgot the login details somewhere along the way.If there's one number in this whole exercise worth sitting with, it's this: the official Sports Department, Government of Rajasthan hasn't posted on Facebook since April 14, 2012.Fourteen years, through Arundhati Choudhary's Commonwealth gold and everything else that's happened in Rajasthan sport since.Its X account's last original post predates a retweet from March 2021, and there's no Instagram at all. A parallel handle, the Rajasthan State Sports Council, exists across all three platforms and is barely livelier.Somewhere behind Choudhary's medal is a genuinely good story, but it just hasn't found a home on the one page built to tell it.Gulveer Singh managed both a silver and a bronze for Uttar Pradesh this Games, a rare double that would make a great centrepiece for the state's sporting year. Instead, across two separate official handles on three platforms, Uttar Pradesh Sports has produced little beyond reposts, while its sister account, Sports Directorate, Govt of Uttar Pradesh, hasn't posted at all in 2026.Delhi Government, for its part, doesn't run a dedicated sports account at all on any of the popular social media platforms, so gold medalist Harsh Singh and bronze medalist Tejaswin Shankar, both representing India's capital, don't really have an institutional cheerleader online, their wins quietly absorbed into the general churn of city government updates. Both athletes are, in effect, doing their own promotional legwork.Set against all that quiet, Tamil Nadu feels like a different sport altogether. Its Sports Tamil Nadu handles post multiple times a day, celebrating not just its own three medalists, Praveen Chithravel, Selva Prabhu, Muthupandi Raja, but athletes from other states too, weaving in government scheme updates without it ever reading like bureaucracy.Every medallist got a dedicated post. Somewhere in Tamil Nadu, a kid training in long jump or wrestling doesn't have to wonder whether the sport leads anywhere. The state tells them, publicly, almost daily.Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka's Facebook and Instagram pages, Assam, Bihar, and Tripura all follow a version of that same habit, active, consistent, generous with attention toward athletes nobody outside their district would otherwise know existed.Kerala doesn't run a separate sports handle on X but keeps its Facebook and Instagram genuinely lively, making sure Murali Sreeshankar and Mohammed Basil's silvers got their due.Andhra Pradesh mirrors that same rhythm across all three platforms.Not every state falls neatly into being inactive or staying proactive. Punjab's account managed just two posts on X all year, New Year's and Republic Day, though its Facebook and Instagram carry a bit more life around coaching and departmental meetings, even if athletes rarely get top billing.Uttarakhand was genuinely active last year before cooling off in 2026, leaning more toward government scheme announcements on Facebook, though its Instagram at least carried two posts around the Games.Maharashtra has dedicated posts up for both Sarvesh Kushare and Dilip Gavit, with Instagram staying fairly regular, enough effort to stay out of the quiet column.Karnataka's X account hasn't posted since March 2024, around an unrelated cultural-team event, even though its Facebook and Instagram have stayed warm and active toward its CWG medalists.It is worth asking why this actually matters, beyond good manners. Well, a state sports department's social media feed isn't just a courtesy board for congratulations; it's one of the cheapest, most direct tools available to build the next generation of athletes.A youngster in a small town is far more likely to pick up a javelin because they saw a state government post celebrating someone from their own district. Even when it comes to promoting any government policy, social media can be as effective.Visibility drives aspiration. There's a funding logic too. Sponsors, corporates, and even state finance departments allocate resources partly based on visible public interest, and a well-run social account is often the easiest evidence a sport has that interest.ALSO READ: Anahat Singh: What is in the name? A word from Guru Nanak's prayer, now India's squash sensation Silence, on the other hand, sends the message that grassroots sport isn't a priority worth the effort of a single post, even when the state has just produced a medallist on the world stage.It is worth it because sometimes, the first step towards building a sporting culture is simply showing people that their achievements are being seen.
Article Summary: India won 39 medals at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Haryana produced 11 medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze. But the state sports department has posted just once in all of 2026. What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Government funding or social media presence? Article Title: ‘That video was not ordinary’: PM Modi praises Lovlina for objecting to distorted India map - Watch
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi shares a light moment with boxer Lovlina Borgohain. (PTI Photo)

‘That video was not ordinary’

Mirabai opens up about four difficult years

Narender's joke leaves Modi laughing

NEW DELHI: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain's decision to object to a distorted Indian map during the Commonwealth Games earned special appreciation from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time.Lovlina, who won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow, was among India's medal winners who interacted with Modi at his residence on Sunday. The meeting, attended by Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Minister of State for Sports Raksha Khadse and Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha, saw athletes recount their experiences from the Games in an informal and emotional setting.In a little over 10-minute video of the interaction shared by the Prime Minister's Office on Monday, Modi brought up Lovlina's confrontation with a restaurant in Glasgow after she noticed a distorted Indian map.“Kya hua wo restaurant waale se jhagda kar rahi thi? (What happened, you were fighting with that restaurant guy?)” Modi asked.Lovlina laughed before explaining why she intervened.“We had such a good performance and it was the last day of the Games. It was a happy occasion sir, we were celebrating and I didn't like it when I saw the distorted map. I politely told them and they have made the changes also,” she explained.Modi applauded the boxer for noticing the issue despite being in the middle of celebrations after her medal-winning campaign.“To be able to recognise the significance of that map at a time when you were celebrating and the Games were over, I can tell you truthfully, that video was not ordinary. It will be remembered by people for a very long time,” he told the Tokyo Olympics bronze medallist.India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.The interaction also provided an emotional window into Mirabai Chanu's journey to her gold medal in the women's 48kg category. The weightlifter produced a Games-record lift of 190kg, but her triumph came after four difficult years following her one-kilogram miss at the Paris Olympics. Modi asked Mirabai about the tears she shed on the podium and even fed her a laddu during their interaction.“Itne aansu tapak rahe the (So many tears were rolling down),” Modi remarked.Mirabai explained that the tears represented years of accumulated emotions.“I was very happy and emotional at that moment. I was crying because I missed a medal in the Paris Olympics by one kilogram. I have faced a lot in these last four years. I was battling injuries and some family problems too.“There were a lot of things. So, these four years were very tough for me. And when I stood on the podium, our flag went up and the anthem played, it was hard to stop myself,” she said.The meeting also had its lighter moments. Boxer Narender Berwal, who won silver in the +90kg category, recalled a funny exchange with a Pakistani boxer after beating him at the 2015 World Military Games.“During the 2015 World Military Games, I had a bout with a Pakistani boxer. I won it but when we were together in the medical room for treatment to our niggles, he said to me 'Bhaijan aapka naam Narender hai, aapke coach ka naam Narender hai, aapke Pradhan Mantri ka naam Narender hai, mujhe Narender naam se nafrat ho gayi hai.' (Brother, you, your coach and your PM are all named Narender. I hate this name now),” he recalled, drawing laughter from Modi.The Prime Minister also underlined the broader significance of the athletes' achievements, saying their medals were helping inspire a new generation.“I have been in this house for 12-13 years now and if there is one group that I have met regularly here, it is the athletes because of your efforts to win medals for India and your tradition of scaling new heights.“Far more than our push to promote sports in schools, it is your medals that inspire people,” Modi said.
Article Summary: Lovlina Borgohain won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow. Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time. India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.

Article Title: ‘From every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping’: PM Modi’s heartfelt message to CWG heroes - Watch
Article Text:
PM Narendra Modi interacted with India's CWG 2026 medal winners at his residence on Sunday. (Pic credit: PM Modi's X post)

Mirabai recalls four years of struggle

‘One family will bring three medals’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s Glasgow success

NEW DELHI: “From every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping.”Prime Minister Narendra Modi had an emotional message for Mirabai Chanu as he interacted with India's Commonwealth Games 2026 medal winners at his residence on Sunday, reflecting on the sacrifices behind the country's successful campaign in Glasgow.Modi hosted the medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg and heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys at the Games. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze, finishing fourth in the overall standings.During one of the conversations, Modi recalled the emotional scenes surrounding Mirabai's gold-medal triumph.“Tears were falling from you. I feel as if from every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping,” Modi told the Olympic silver medallist.Mirabai, who won gold in Glasgow, opened up about the difficult journey that preceded her Commonwealth Games triumph, including the disappointment of the Paris Olympics.“I was very happy, and emotional too. That day the happiness was greater and I cried because at the Paris Olympics, I lost a medal by 1 kg. In a player’s life what all we have to face. So within these 4 years, how much and what all I had faced, every time injuries were going on and all that was happening.So with great difficulty I had faced these 4 years. So when all that happened, on the podium when I stood, sir, and when our flag goes up and our national anthem plays, sir, we cannot stop, sir, tears come out on their own,” she said.Modi responded by highlighting the wider impact of the athletes' achievements.“This is very good. It is not as if this achievement of yours is considered only your achievement; your victory becomes a very big inspiration for the coming generations.”The informal interaction also saw athletes share lighter and deeply personal moments from their Glasgow campaigns.Modi reminded para shot put gold medallist Sharmila Dhankar of a promise she had made earlier.“You made a promise. Last time, yours, both daughters will become players,” Modi said with a smile.Dhankar replied: “Haanji, right now they are young in age. In the next Commonwealth, one family will bring 3 medals.”Men's 100m T47 gold medallist Dilip Gavit, meanwhile, spoke about dedicating his performance to his guru.“When I was running, when my event was on 29th (July), that day was Guru Purnima, so that day I gave a gift to my guru,” he was heard saying in the video.In another video posted by Modi, gold medallist boxer Sakshi Chaudhary introduced herself and the contingent.“Hello friends! This is Sakshi Chaudhary. Today, our honourable Prime Minister has invited us, the Commonwealth Games medalists, and we feel very proud. We are extremely happy to have met him; he is very humble. Sir, would you like to say something?” she said.Modi replied with a message that summed up his interaction with the athletes: “Jo khelega, woh khilega” (The one who plays, will blossom). “Always cheer for Bharat.”India's fourth-place finish came despite a significantly smaller contingent and a reduced sporting programme compared to Birmingham 2022. India sent 122 athletes to Glasgow, compared to 210 in Birmingham, while 30 of its 61 medals in 2022 came in sports that were not part of the Glasgow programme.Despite those limitations, India retained its fourth-place position and improved its medal conversion rate, with 38 athletes returning home with medals. Long-distance runner Gulveer Singh was the only Indian athlete to win two medals.The Glasgow Games concluded after 11 days, with Scotland handing over the Commonwealth Games flag and ceremonial baton to India ahead of the 2030 edition in Ahmedabad.The symbols were handed to Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra, Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha and Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi during the closing ceremony.Ahmedabad will become only the second Indian city to host the Commonwealth Games after New Delhi staged the 2010 edition.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi hosted medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg. Modi heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze.
